# A newborn split tab container flashes its overflow control for one frame

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` — "the real tour keeps density, data, Canvas output, themes, rails, and identities live" — frame-samples the dense tour with a rAF monitor and asserts `the projection never leaks duplicate overflow controls` (`overflowControlDuplicateFrames === 0`). With #19086's test-side fixes in place the tour reaches that assertion for the first time since the dark-splitter red began masking it, and it reds deterministically: in every run that reached the monitor (3 of 3, 2026-09-23 08:50–09:11Z, branch `test/19086-dark-splitter-theme-reveal` on `dev@9dcc4ef088`, own Neural Link bridge per #19066) exactly ONE sampled frame of ~843 shows two visible `.neo-tab-overflow-control` elements, always during the same beat: `splitNode(security → below scale): promote through the shipped semantic operation` (pip 5).

## The Problem

The monitor's sample, with exact owners (each control is its toolbar's own action contribution, `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs` `createActionControl()` → `owner.addActionContribution(...)`, so `control.closest('.neo-tab-header-toolbar')` is authoritative):

```
owners: [
  {containerId: 'neo-tab-container-7', controlId: 'neo-button-103', toolbarId: 'neo-tab-header-toolbar-18',
   tabs: ['Security Signal Center'], toolbarRect: [332, 874, 954, 33]},
  {containerId: 'neo-tab-container-3', controlId: 'neo-button-36',  toolbarId: 'neo-tab-header-toolbar-4',
   tabs: ['Priority Alert Observatory', … 11 tabs], toolbarRect: [1292, 121, 881, 33]}
]
```

The second is the heavy group's steady control (it overflows at every width; 842 frames show exactly one control, this one). The first is the container `splitNode` just created for the promoted Security pane: one tab, a 954 px header — nothing to overflow — and for one frame its `⋯` control is mounted and visible. It is gone on the next sample. The earlier build of this sampler attributed the control to the Metrics toolbar by a nearest-rect heuristic; that attribution was wrong and is replaced in #19086's PR.

Observation vs inference: the one-frame double is observed. Which projection step paints the newborn container's control before its first split verdict hides it is not yet classified.

## The Architectural Reality

- The runtime overflow plugin measures natural widths on mount and applies a visible/hidden split per projection (`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs` `project()` :677, `applySplit()` :905, `syncControl()` :1107). Its control is created `hidden: true` (`createActionControl()` :1068) and is meant to surface only when `hidden.length > 0`; a single active tab is never hidden (`active-never-hidden`, :69–138), so this container must never show the control at all.
- The dock projection births the promoted pane's `tab.Container` inside `splitNode`; the plugin runs `project(true)` from `onOwnerMounted()` (:371–397) and again on `insert` / `remove` / `moveTo` / `resize`. A control that is visible for one frame means a projection step un-hid it before the split verdict for the newborn header landed — candidates: the newborn toolbar inheriting the source header's action state (the Security tab leaves the heavy group, whose control IS visible), or a first measure pass reading a zero-extent strip.
- The dense witness holds this contract on purpose: duplicate overflow controls were a shipped defect class of the projection (the assertion dates from #15136), so a one-frame return of it is a regression against a guarded contract even though a 16 ms flash is at the edge of perception.

## Classification (2026-09-23, instrumented dense-tour runs 10:26–10:35Z on the seat's own bridge)

**The plugin's verdict was never wrong; the dock reconciler un-hid the control from outside.** A static birth log on the plugin recorded the newborn toolbar's (`neo-tab-header-toolbar-18`) five `project` passes at the `splitNode` beat: every one computed `hidden: []` (extent 930–1075 px, one item of 136 px natural width, `activeItemId` present, `activeIndex` 0, tab container wired) — yet `control.hidden` read `false` at the start of the fourth pass, and the fifth pass hid it again. A `hidden` observer on the control then named the writer with its stack: `src/dashboard/dock/projection/Reconciler.mjs:612` inside `reconcileProjection` (`overflowPlugins.forEach(plugin => plugin.control?.hidden && (plugin.control.hidden = false))`, called from `Workspace.refreshDockWorkspace`), which restores every overflow control to visible after a staged shell swap and only then awaits each plugin's `project(true)`. That restore dates from #15136 (2026-07-14), when the control was a floating button hidden for transport during native reparenting (the `hideMode: 'visibility'` hold at `:773`). In action mode — what the dock's header rail installs (`LayoutAdapter.mjs`, `projectAsAction: true`) — the control is a toolbar contribution whose visibility is the plugin's verdict, so the forced un-hide shows a control with nothing to show until the recapture's two DOM round trips land (~6 ms later, one frame). Steady non-overflowing toolbars receive the same un-hide but re-hide before a paint; the newborn's recapture includes a natural-width restore round trip, which is why its frame is painted. The in-place projection branch (`:430–437`) never had the un-hide.

## The Fix

`Reconciler.reconcileProjection` restores only floating-mode controls (`!plugin.projectAsAction`) after a swap; an action-mode control's visibility stays the plugin's verdict, decided by the recapture that follows. A red-first unit arm in `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockProjectionReconciler.spec.mjs` creates the action-mode control on a retained tab, stages a three-child split swap and asserts no visible transition and `control.hidden === true` afterwards (red without the fix: a `false` transition received). The dense witness is the runtime receipt: `WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` "the real tour keeps density…" passes its `overflowControlDuplicateFrames` assertion in three consecutive runs (#19086's press/monitor fixes are required to reach it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 The projection step that shows the newborn container's control before its first split verdict is named here, with the frame's plugin state as evidence.
- [ ] AC-2 A container born by `splitNode` with one tab never mounts a visible `.neo-tab-overflow-control`: the dense witness's duplicate-overflow assertion passes in three consecutive whole-file runs of `WorkstationNL.spec.mjs` on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-3 The heavy group's steady control and the overflow menu keep their behaviour (`counts['1'] > 0` still observed; the existing overflow arms stay green).

## Out of Scope

- #19086 (the press and monitor fixes that unmasked this; its PR carries them).
- The dense witness's Canvas-pixel receipt (`the exact scale Canvas changes after its worker receives new data`) — promoted to #19110 (12 of 16 runs on 2026-09-23), independent of this frame.
